title: Vedanta lines up $25 bn investment over next three years for organic growth
description:
The Vedanta Group has lined up USD 25 billion in investments over the next three years to expand capacities across its existing businesses through organic growth and brownfield expansions, a top company official said.
Vedanta founder and chairman Anil Agarwal, who was in the city on Wednesday, said the conglomerate would focus on its existing assets for growth, while remaining open to acquiring public sector assets if opportunities arise.
"Current capex plans are for organic growth in aluminium, copper, zinc, oil and gas. All will be brownfield expansions," he said.
"We are going to invest around USD 25 billion," Agarwal said.
The capital expenditure would also support Vedanta's ambition to become one of the world's largest mining companies in critical metals, and emerge as a leading silver producer within three to four years, he said.
The group, which comprises 10 major companies, aims to grow its overall business from USD 30 billion to USD 50 billion within three years, Agarwal
